title: Java Slide 4
description: Practice exam covering Java selection statements (if, if...else, conditional operator), while iteration, counter- and sentinel-controlled loops, type conversion and promotion, compound assignment operators, prefix/postfix increment and decrement operators, and primitive type defaults.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet executes?
questions.explanation: The postfix operator c++ uses the current value of c (5) in the first printf before incrementing c to 6, whereas the prefix operator ++c increments c from 6 to 7 before using the new value in the third printf.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet executes?
questions.explanation: Dividing two int values (7 / 4) performs integer division, which truncates the fractional part .75 to yield 1 rather than rounding to 2, while 7 % 4 evaluates to the remainder 3.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet executes?
questions.explanation: Starting from 3, each iteration of the while loop multiplies product by 3 to produce 9, 27, 81, and finally 243, at which point product <= 100 becomes false and the loop terminates.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet executes?
questions.explanation: The compound assignment c += 7 is equivalent to c = c + 7 (assigning 10 to c), and g %= 9 is equivalent to g = g % 9 (assigning the remainder 3 to g).

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet executes?
questions.explanation: In avg1, the unary cast operator (double) has higher precedence than /, so total is converted to 257.0 and gradeCounter is promoted to 3.0, yielding 85.67 when formatted with %.2f. In avg2, parentheses force integer division (257 / 3 = 85) before the cast to double, printing 85.00.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet executes?
questions.explanation: The semicolon immediately after the first if (grade >= 60); creates an empty statement as the if body, so bonus += 10; executes unconditionally and sets bonus to 10. In the second if, the omitted braces cause the dangling else to attach to the inner if (grade >= 80), so when the outer condition grade >= 60 is false, the entire nested if...else is skipped.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the main method of the Student class executes?
questions.explanation: Instance variable average defaults to 0.0. Calling s.setAverage(85.0) updates s.average to 85.0, and the subsequent invalid call s.setAverage(105.0) fails the average <= 100.0 check, leaving s.average unchanged at 85.0 (grade B). For s2, -10.0 fails average > 0.0 in the constructor, keeping the default 0.0 (grade F).

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet executes?
questions.explanation: Because studentCounter starts at 1 and increases by 2 each iteration (taking values 1, 3, and 5), studentCounter % 2 != 0 is always true, incrementing passes 3 times and leaving failures at 0. On the third iteration, studentCounter += 2 updates studentCounter from 5 to 7 before the loop terminates, and passes > 2 evaluates to "Bonus".

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet executes?
questions.explanation: In a++ + 4 < --b, a++ yields 3 (then a becomes 4) so 3 + 4 is 7, and --b decrements b to 7 first; since 7 < 7 is false, the third operand b + a / 2 evaluates using the updated values 7 + 4 / 2 = 9, making c += 9 equal to 11. In the second conditional expression, c >= 10 is true, so c / 4 is evaluated using integer division (11 / 4 = 2) before being promoted to double (2.00).

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet executes?
questions.explanation: Compound assignment operators associate from right to left, so x -= y += step first updates y = y + step and then subtracts that new value of y from x. Tracing the three iterations yields: Iteration 1 (24 % 3 == 0 -> step = 2, y = 5, x = 19, count = 1); Iteration 2 (19 % 3 != 0 -> step = 3, y = 8, x = 11, count = 2); Iteration 3 (11 % 3 != 0 -> step = 3, y = 11, x = 0, count = 3), after which 0 > 11 is false.
